sanskrit: ima indrāya sunvire somāso dadhyāśiraḥ . tāṃ ā madāya vajrahasta pītaye haribhyāṃ yāhyoka ā
english: These soma draughts mixed with curds have been pressed out for Indra. Come to them, O thunderbolt-bearing one, for exhilaration and drinking — come home with your two bay horses.

sanskrit: ima indra madāya te somāścikitra ukithanaḥ . madhoḥ papāna upa no giraḥ śṛṇu rāsva stotrāya girvaṇaḥ
english: These soma juices, O Indra, bright and rich in sacred verse, have been pressed for your delight. Having drunk of the sweet, hear our hymns and give bounty to our praise, O lover of song.

sanskrit: ā tvā3dya sabardughāṃ huve gāyatravepasam . indraṃ dhenuṃ sudughāmanyāmiṣamurudhārāmaraṅkṛtam
english: Today I call you who are born of the Gāyatrī hymn, you who are like a milch-cow yielding abundance — Indra, the divine milch-cow, another one yielding good milk, whose streams are broad and who is well prepared.

sanskrit: na tvā bṛhanto adrayo varanta indra vīḍavaḥ . yacchikṣasi stuvate māvate vasu na kiṣṭadā mināti te
english: Not the great and solid mountains hold you back, O Indra. When you bestow wealth upon the one who praises you and worships you, no adversary diminishes your gift.

sanskrit: ka īṃ veda sute sacā pibantaṃ kadvayo dadhe . ayaṃ yaḥ puro vibhinatyojasā mandānaḥ śipryandhasaḥ
english: Who knows him drinking companionably at the soma pressing? Who has set him as a twin? He is this one who shatters cities with his strength, who grows exhilarated from the juice that touches his cheeks.

sanskrit: yadindra śāso avrataṃ cyāvayā sadasaspari . asmākamaṃśuṃ maghavanpuruspṛhaṃ vasavye adhi barhaya
english: When, O Indra, you drive away from the seat the one who transgresses your command, O Maghavan, place our soma stalk — the one widely coveted — upon the sacrificial grass for the winning of wealth.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā no daivyaṃ vacaḥ parjanyo brahmaṇaspatiḥ . putrairbhrātṛbhiraditirnu pātu no duṣṭaraṃ trāmaṇaṃ vacaḥ
english: May Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya, and Brahmaṇaspati protect our divine speech. May Aditi with her sons and brothers protect us — our speech that is hard to cross and that is our refuge.

sanskrit: kadā ca na starīrasi nendra saścasi dāśuṣe . upopennu maghavanbhūya innu te dānaṃ devasya pṛcyate
english: Never are you barren, O Indra, and you do not abandon the devout worshipper. O Maghavan, you become ever more abundant — truly, the gift of the divine one is extolled.

sanskrit: yuṅkṣvā hi vṛtrahantama harī indra parāvataḥ . arvācīno maghavantsomapītaya ugra ṛṣvebhirā gahi
english: Yoke your two bay horses, O Indra, greatest destroyer of Vṛtra, from the distant realm. Come near, O Maghavan, come here with your great steeds to drink the soma, O mighty one.

sanskrit: tvāmidā hyo naro 'pīpyanvajrinbhūrṇayaḥ . sa indra stomavāhasa iha śrudhyupa svasaramā gahi
english: You indeed, O thunderbolt-bearer, the men of abundant gifts enriched yesterday. So, O Indra, bearer of praise-songs, hear here — come to your own dwelling.

sanskrit: apo mahī vṛṇute cakṣuṣā tamo jyotiṣkṛṇoti sūnari
english: The great waters cover darkness with the eye of sight; the skilled one makes light.

sanskrit: imā u vāṃ diviṣṭaya usrā havante aśvinā . ayaṃ vāmahve 'vase śacīvasū viśaṃviśaṃ hi gacchathaḥ
english: These dawning invocations at daybreak call to you both, O Aśvins. I here invoke you both for help, O you rich in powers — for you go to every clan.

sanskrit: ku ṣṭhaḥ ko vāmaśvinā tapāno devā martyaḥ . ghnatā vāmaśmayā kṣapāmāṇoṃśunetthamu ādunyathā
english: Where are you, O Aśvins? Which mortal burns for you, O gods? Striking with your stony weapon by night, pressing out the soma-stalk — thus indeed you have come to him.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vāṃ madhumattamaḥ sutaḥ somo diviṣṭiṣu . tamaśvinā pibataṃ tiro ahnyaṃ dhattaṃ ratnāni dāśuṣe
english: This soma, most rich in sweetness, has been pressed for you both at the heavenly invocations. Drink it, O Aśvins, through the days and nights; bestow treasures upon the devout worshipper.

sanskrit: ā tvā somasya galdayā sadā yācannahaṃ jyā . bhūrṇiṃ mṛgaṃ na savaneṣu cukrudhaṃ ka īśānaṃ na yāciṣat
english: I, the bowstring, always seeking you by the stream of soma — I have made the fierce one, like a wild beast, angry at the soma pressings. Who would not entreat the sovereign one?

sanskrit: adhvaryo drāvayā tvaṃ somamindraḥ pipāsati . upo nūnaṃ yuyuje vṛṣṇā harī ā ca jagāma vṛtrahā
english: O Adhvaryu priest, pour out the soma swiftly — Indra thirsts. Now indeed he has yoked his two powerful bay horses and the Vṛtra-slayer has come here.

sanskrit: abhī ṣatastadā bharendra jyāyaḥ kanīyasaḥ . purūvasurhi maghavanbabhūvitha bharebhare ca havyaḥ
english: Bring then what surpasses that, O Indra — the greater beyond the lesser. For you have become Purūvasu, O Maghavan, and you are to be invoked in every battle and every conflict.

sanskrit: yadindra yāvatastvametāvadahamīśīya . stotāramiddadhiṣe radāvaso na pāpatvāya raṃsiṣam
english: O Indra, if I were master of as much as you are master of, I would hold the praiser alone and I would not take delight in evil, O giver of wealth.

sanskrit: tvamindra pratūrtiṣvabhi viśvā asi spṛdhaḥ . aśastihā janitā vṛtratūrasi tvaṃ tūrya taruṣyataḥ
english: You, O Indra, surpass all rivals in swift attacks. You are the slayer of the slanderer, the creator, the swift one who breaks through Vṛtra — you are the swift one who overcomes the attacker.

sanskrit: pra yo ririkṣa ojasā divaḥ sadobhyaspari . na tvā vivyāca raja indra pārthivamati viśvaṃ vavakṣitha
english: He who has grown beyond the seats of heaven by his might — no earthly realm has encompassed you, O Indra; you have extended beyond all the universe.

sanskrit: bodhāmasi tvā haryaśva yajñairbodhā na stomamandhaso madeṣu
english: We waken you, O lord of bay horses, with sacrifices; waken, as with a hymn, in the exhilarations of the soma juice.

sanskrit: yoniṣṭa indra sadane akāri tamā nṛbhiḥ purūhūta pra yāhi . aso yathā no 'vitā vṛdhaściddado vasūni mamadaśca somaiḥ
english: Your seat, O Indra, has been made ready in the place of sacrifice — come forward thither with the men, O much-invoked one. Be our protector and our increaser; give us riches and be gladdened by the soma.

sanskrit: adardarutsamasṛjo vi khāni tvamarṇavānbadbadhānāṃ aramṇāḥ . mahāntamindra parvataṃ vi yadvaḥ sṛjaddhārā ava yaddānavānhan
english: You burst open the fountains and released their streams; you set free the floods that were bound and confined. When you, O Indra, split open the great mountain and let the streams flow down, when you smote the Dānavas.

sanskrit: suṣvāṇāsa indra stumasi tvā saniṣyantaścittuvinṛmṇa vājam . ā no bhara suvitaṃ yasya konā tanā tmanā sahyāmā tvotāḥ
english: We who have pressed the soma, O Indra, praise you hoping to win the prize, O you whose wealth is prominently known. Bring to us good fortune whose shelter we may achieve with our bodies — may we be strengthened by your aid.

sanskrit: jagṛhmā te dakṣiṇamindra hastaṃ vasūyavo vasupate vasūnām . vidmā hi tvā gopatiṃ śūra gonāmasmabhyaṃ citraṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ rayindāḥ
english: We have grasped your right hand, O Indra, longing for wealth, O lord of wealth. For we know you as the bull-lord of cattle, O hero — give us brilliant, bountiful riches.

sanskrit: indraṃ naro nemadhitā havanti yatpāryā yunajate dhiyastāḥ . śūro nṛṣātā śravasaśca kāma ā gomati vraje bhajā tvaṃ naḥ
english: The men invoke Indra with devoted worship when those prayers that are appointed are yoked. The hero who conquers men, who loves glory — give us a share in the cattle-pen full of cows.

sanskrit: vayaḥ suparṇā upa sedurindraṃ priyamedhā ṛṣayo nādhamānāḥ . apa dhvāntamūrṇuhi pūrdhi cakṣurmumugdhyā3smānnidhayeva baddhān
english: The birds with beautiful wings, the beloved-wisdom sages, calling upon him, have approached Indra. Roll away the darkness, fill the eye with sight, release us as if we were bound in traps.

sanskrit: nāke suparṇamupa yatpatantaṃ hṛdā venanto abhyacakṣata tvā . hiraṇyapakṣaṃ varuṇasya dūtaṃ yamasya yonau śakunaṃ bhuraṇyum
english: Upon the vault of heaven, as the beautiful-winged one flew, those longing in their hearts gazed upon you. The golden-winged bird, messenger of Varuṇa, the restless bird in the womb of Yama.

sanskrit: brahma jajñānaṃ prathamaṃ purastādvi sīmataḥ suruco vena āvaḥ . sa budhnyā upamā asya viṣṭhāḥ sataśca yonimasataśca vivaḥ
english: The first-born brahman from the east — the seeker revealed the shining one beyond the boundary. He, the highest, pervades all the foundations of this one; he opened the womb of both the existent and the nonexistent.

sanskrit: apūrvyā purutamānyasmai mahe vīrāya tavase turāya . virapśine vajriṇe śantamāni vacāṃsyāsmai sthavirāya takṣuḥ
english: For him who is without precedent, the most manifold — for this great hero, the mighty, the swift — for the powerful one, the thunderbolt-bearer, the most beneficent, they have fashioned these words for him, the firm one.

sanskrit: āvattamindraḥ śacyā dhamantamapa snīhitiṃ nṛmaṇā adhadrāḥ
english: Indra by his power drove away the one who was blowing — he, the man-minded one, blew away the sticky hindrance.

sanskrit: vṛtrasya tvā śvasathādīṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahurye sakhāyaḥ . marudbhirindra sakhyaṃ te astvathemā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi
english: Frightened by Vṛtra's hissing, all the gods who were your companions abandoned you. Let friendship between you and the Maruts exist, O Indra — and thus you shall conquer all these armies.

sanskrit: vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ samane bahūnāṃ yuvānaṃ santaṃ palito jagāra . devasya paśya kāvyaṃ mahitvādyā mamāra sa hyaḥ samāna
english: The gray-haired one swallowed the vigorous youth who was trembling in the assembly of many. Behold the power of the divine sage — he died today who was alive yesterday in the same assembly.

sanskrit: tvaṃ ha tyatsaptabhyo jāyamāno 'śatrubhyo abhavaḥ śatrurindra . gūḍhe dyāvāpṛthivī anvavindo vibhumadbhyo bhuvanebhyo raṇaṃ dhāḥ
english: You, O Indra, being born among the seven, became an enemy to those who had no enemy. You found heaven and earth in their hidden place and waged war with the wide-extended worlds.

sanskrit: meḍiṃ na tvā vajriṇaṃ bhṛṣṭimantaṃ purudhasmānaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ sthirapsnum . karoṣyaryastaruṣīrduvasyurindra dyukṣaṃ vṛtrahaṇaṃ gṛṇīṣe
english: Like a pillar — you, the thunderbolt-bearer, the sharp one, the manifoldly renowned, the bull, firm in nourishment — you make your enemies yield, O Indra who desires to serve; I sing of the brilliant Vṛtra-slayer.

sanskrit: pra vo mahe mahevṛdhe bharadhvaṃ pracetase pra sumatiṃ kṛṇudhvam . viśaḥ pūrvīḥ pra cara carṣaṇiprāḥ
english: Bring forth praise to the great one, the greatly increasing, the far-sighted one; render good thought. Go forward through the many peoples, O you who fills all living beings.

sanskrit: śunaṃ huvema maghavānamindramasminbhare nṛtamaṃ vājasātau . śṛṇvantamugramūtaye samatsu dhnantaṃ vṛtrāṇi sañjitaṃ dhanāni
english: We would invoke for good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most manly in this battle, in the winning of prizes — the mighty one who listens, for our aid in conflicts, smiting the Vṛtras, winning wealth together.

sanskrit: udu brahmāṇyairata śravasyendraṃ samarye mahayā vasiṣṭha . ā yo viśvāni śravasā tatānopaśrotā ma īvato vacāṃsi
english: Rise up, send forth the brahman prayers seeking glory; magnify Indra in the battle, O Vasiṣṭha. He who has stretched forth all things with his fame — may he hear my words as they approach.

sanskrit: cakraṃ yadasyāpsvā niṣattamuto tadasmai madhviccacchadyāt . pṛthivyāmatiṣitaṃ yadūdhaḥ payo goṣvadadhā oṣadhīṣu
english: The wheel set in the waters — let that sweet thing please him. The udder that is stretched upon the earth — the milk he placed in the cows and in the plants.

sanskrit: ariṣṭanemiṃ pṛtanājamāśuṃ svastaye tārkṣyamihā huvema
english: We invoke here for our well-being Tārkṣya, the swift one who goes into battle, whose wheel-rim is unharmed.

sanskrit: trātāramindramavitāramindraṃ havehave suhavaṃ śūramindram . huve nu śakraṃ puruhūtamindramidaṃ havirmaghavā vetvindraḥ
english: Indra the protector, Indra the helper, the easy-to-invoke warrior Indra in every invocation — I now invoke the mighty Indra, the much-invoked. May Indra the bountiful one take this oblation.

sanskrit: yajāmaha indraṃ vajradakṣiṇaṃ harīṇāṃ rathya3ṃ vivratānām . pra śmaśrubhirdodhuvadūrdhvadhā bhuvadvi senābhirbhayamāno vi rādhasā
english: We worship Indra with the thunderbolt in his right hand, the charioteer of the bay steeds of many ways. He who shakes his beard upward and onward, becoming terrible with his armies, advancing with his bounties.

sanskrit: satrāhaṇaṃ dādhṛṣiṃ tumramindraṃ mahāmapāraṃ vṛśabhaṃ suvajram . hantā yo vṛtraṃ sanitota vājaṃ dātā maghāni maghavā surādhāḥ
english: The all-smiting, the bold, the loud-voiced Indra, the great, the boundless, the bull, bearer of the fine thunderbolt — the slayer of Vṛtra who wins the prize, the bountiful Maghavan who gives riches, the excellent bestower.

sanskrit: yo no vanuṣyannabhidāti marta ugaṇā vā manyamānasturo vā . kṣidhī yudhā śavasā vā tamindrābhī ṣyāma vṛṣamaṇastvotāḥ
english: Whatever mortal assails us wishing to harm us, whether thinking himself fierce or swift — destroy him in battle, or with your strength, O Indra; may we overcome him, protected by your heroic might.

sanskrit: yaṃ vṛtreṣu kṣitaya spardhamānā yaṃ yukteṣu turayanto havante . yaṃ śūrasātau yamapāmupajmanyaṃ viprāso vājayante sa indraḥ
english: He whom the peoples striving against Vṛtras invoke, whom those rushing in the yokings invoke, whom they invoke in the winning of heroes, whom the inspired ones urge on in the contest at the water's proximity — he is Indra.

sanskrit: indrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena vāmīriṣa ā vahataṃ suvīrāḥ . vītaṃ havyānyadhvareṣu devā vardhethāṃ gīrbhīriḍayā madantā
english: O Indra and Parvata, bring here with your great chariot good nourishment, O you of good heroes. Enjoy the oblations at the sacrifice, O gods; grow great, gladdened with songs and praises.

sanskrit: indrāya giro aniśitasargā apaḥ prairayatsagarasya budhnāt . yo akṣeṇeva cakriyau śacībhirviṣvaktastambha pṛthivīmuta dyām
english: For Indra, the songs unleashed like darting streams sent forth the waters from the bottom of the ocean. He who, like an axle by his powers, has everywhere propped up the earth and heaven.

sanskrit: ā tvā sakhāyaḥ sakhyā vavṛtyustiraḥ purū cidarṇavāṃ jagamyāḥ . piturnapātamā dadhita vedhā asminkṣaye pratarāṃ dīdyānaḥ
english: Friends have turned you with friendship; you have gone across many floods indeed. The wise one should take hold of the father's grandson; shining more brightly in this dwelling.

sanskrit: ko adya yuṅkte dhuri gā ṛtasya śimīvato bhāmino durhṛṇāyūn . āsanneṣāmapsuvāho mayobhūnya eṣāṃ bhṛtyāmṛṇadhatsa jīvāt
english: Who today yokes the cattle of cosmic order to the yoke — the laboring, angry, ill-willed ones? The water-bearing one who brings welfare is near to them; he alone who paid the debt of their nurture shall live.
